  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

messages.preview: The `loadModule` mechanism injects mocks as `var` preamble declarations. Now let me check cross-file impact, CI workflow config, and the CRAP gate:

blocks.text:
The `loadModule` injects mocks as `var Java = _testMocks_["Java"]` — so `var Java = {}` shadows the global inside the module wrapper. In the module, `typeof Java !== 'undefined'` — since `var Java` is declared in the function scope, `typeof Java` is defined (var hoisting), even when the mock is `{}`. Wait — important subtlety: when `loadReporter()` is called WITHOUT a Java override, there's no `var Java` preamble declaration, so inside the module `typeof Java` falls back to the actual global. Under node test harness, `Java` is undefined → busy wait. Under dmtools GralJS harness, `Java` global EXISTS → `hasJavaThread()` returns true → `sleepMilliseconds(2)` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real sleep of 2ms. The test asserts `elapsed >= 2` — Thread.sleep(2) sleeps >= 2ms typically, so it passes either way. And the busy-wait test name says "busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable" — under dmtools-java, it's actually NOT busy-waiting; it sleeps via Thread.sleep. The assertion still holds (elapsed >= 2). It's a characterization test that passes in both environments, though semantically it exercises different paths depending on harness. That's OK-ish but worth noting? The test name would be misleading under dmtools-java, but the assertion (elapsed >= 2) is environment-neutral. Hmm, this is a minor nit at most.

But WAIT — there's a real concern for the `hasJavaThread is true only when the Java interop exposes type` test under the dmtools-java harness: `loadReporterWithJava({})` injects `var Java = {}` — shadowing the real global. `hasJavaThread()` → `!!(typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type)` → `typeof Java` — Java is a declared var → 'object'; `Java.type` → undefined → false. Good. And `loadReporterWithJava({ type: function() {...} })` → true. Works in both harnesses.

And `sleepMilliseconds routes positive durations to Thread.sleep under the Java interop` — injects Java mock with `type` function → `sleepViaJavaThread` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(7)` → mock records. Works in both.

Under node harness, `loadReporter()` → no `Java` var → `typeof Java === 'undefined'` → busy wait — correct path.

Under dmtools-java harness, `loadReporter()` → real Java global → hasJavaThread true → Thread.sleep — the sleep happens via Java interop. The test `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` will silently exercise the Java path instead of the busy-wait path in the canonical harness. The busy-wait branch IS covered in the node harness run. Since CI presumably runs both harnesses (ticket: "node and dmtools-java harness green"), coverage-wise the busy-wait branch gets covered by node run. This is a nuance worth a SUGESTION at most.

Actually wait, there's something more important to check — the coverage/crap gate. The crap gate runs via nyc instrument + node harness presumably (per quality.yml). Let me check the quality.yml workflow to see how the crap gate runs, to verify the busy-wait branch is covered there (node harness → Java undefined → busy wait covered). Let me check.

Also check the `while (Date.now() < end) {}` empty loop body — is an empty block statement fine for the code style? Pre-existing.

if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

messages.preview: The `loadModule` mechanism injects mocks as `var` preamble declarations. Now let me check cross-file impact, CI workflow config, and the CRAP gate:

blocks.text:
The `loadModule` injects mocks as `var Java = _testMocks_["Java"]` — so `var Java = {}` shadows the global inside the module wrapper. In the module, `typeof Java !== 'undefined'` — since `var Java` is declared in the function scope, `typeof Java` is defined (var hoisting), even when the mock is `{}`. Wait — important subtlety: when `loadReporter()` is called WITHOUT a Java override, there's no `var Java` preamble declaration, so inside the module `typeof Java` falls back to the actual global. Under node test harness, `Java` is undefined → busy wait. Under dmtools GralJS harness, `Java` global EXISTS → `hasJavaThread()` returns true → `sleepMilliseconds(2)` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real sleep of 2ms. The test asserts `elapsed >= 2` — Thread.sleep(2) sleeps >= 2ms typically, so it passes either way. And the busy-wait test name says "busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable" — under dmtools-java, it's actually NOT busy-waiting; it sleeps via Thread.sleep. The assertion still holds (elapsed >= 2). It's a characterization test that passes in both environments, though semantically it exercises different paths depending on harness. That's OK-ish but worth noting? The test name would be misleading under dmtools-java, but the assertion (elapsed >= 2) is environment-neutral. Hmm, this is a minor nit at most.

But WAIT — there's a real concern for the `hasJavaThread is true only when the Java interop exposes type` test under the dmtools-java harness: `loadReporterWithJava({})` injects `var Java = {}` — shadowing the real global. `hasJavaThread()` → `!!(typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type)` → `typeof Java` — Java is a declared var → 'object'; `Java.type` → undefined → false. Good. And `loadReporterWithJava({ type: function() {...} })` → true. Works in both harnesses.

And `sleepMilliseconds routes positive durations to Thread.sleep under the Java interop` — injects Java mock with `type` function → `sleepViaJavaThread` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(7)` → mock records. Works in both.

Under node harness, `loadReporter()` → no `Java` var → `typeof Java === 'undefined'` → busy wait — correct path.

Under dmtools-java harness, `loadReporter()` → real Java global → hasJavaThread true → Thread.sleep — the sleep happens via Java interop. The test `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` will silently exercise the Java path instead of the busy-wait path in the canonical harness. The busy-wait branch IS covered in the node harness run. Since CI presumably runs both harnesses (ticket: "node and dmtools-java harness green"), coverage-wise the busy-wait branch gets covered by node run. This is a nuance worth a SUGESTION at most.

Actually wait, there's something more important to check — the coverage/crap gate. The crap gate runs via nyc instrument + node harness presumably (per quality.yml). if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

The doc comment says it "Returns true when the tokens sample is a replay that must be skipped" and documents the marking. It's slightly surprising but documented. Style nit — the repo convention seems tolerant. I'd call this SUGESTION.

**d) `parseCacheOptions` still parses logDownloadSleepMs inline** — duplication of sleep-parsing logic now that `parseSleepMilliseconds` exists. Two parsers for the same config value. SUGESTION: reuse. But note subtle difference: `parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0` — for '-3': -3 (truthy negative), vs parseSleepMilliseconds('-3') → 0. Gate is `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` so equivalent behavior. Reusing parseSleepMilliseconds in parseCacheOptions would be safe and would remove duplication. SUGESTION.

Hmm wait, actually let me double check: `parseSleepMilliseconds(null)` → parseInt(null) → NaN → NaN||0 → 0 → max(0,0)=0. `parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0`: null||0 → 0 → 0. Same. `undefined` same. `'500'` → 500 both. OK — equivalent for the > 0 gate. SUGESTION valid.

- `processRunLogs sleeps between downloads...` asserts `elapsed >= 5` — fine with real sleeps. 
- `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits...` asserts `elapsed >= 2` — busy wait guarantees. Under dmtools-java harness the path is Thread.sleep — still >= 2ms. OK.
- `first download must not sleep` asserts `elapsed < 100` with logDownloadSleepMs '500' — on an extremely slow CI, the non-sleep path taking >1s is nearly impossible (single function call). OK.

**f) `hasJavaThread` — `typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type`** — under GralJS, `Java.type` exists. Under node with a mocked `Java = {}` (no type) → false. Matches old behavior. OK.

**g) Export surface**: `sleepViaJavaThread` / `sleepViaBusyWait` NOT exported (unlike other new helpers) — intentional? The convention per PR: "Helpers exported for direct branch coverage". These two are covered indirectly (sleepViaJavaThread via Java mock test; sleepViaBusyWait via loadReporter() under node). Consistent enough — not an issue.

**h) `newUsageTracking` — exports `applyResumeSignal`/`applyRateLimitSignal`? NOT exported** — they're covered via applyLogSignals tests. Fine.

**i) `collectFaSourceKeys(samples)` vs `usageSourceLabel(faSourceKeys)`** — could be one function, but each is trivial; CRAP-driven decomposition explains it. Not an issue.

**j) The comment on `parseResumeSignal`** says "The feedback-loop shape wins when a line matches both" — accurate.

**k) Behavior nit — `applyLogSignals` computes resume/rate-limit regexes on the raw `line` and timeout on `lower`** — matches old code exactly (old used `line.match` and `/i` regexes on line; timeout on lower). Equivalent.

**l) Any scope creep?** No — only the named functions + tests. The ticket allows refactor + tests only. Files changed: exactly 2. Baseline not committed. 

**m) `newUsageTracking()` returned object used with `deepEqual` in test — fine.

**n) Missing test?** — `sleepViaBusyWait` with ms=0? Guarded by duration<=0. `parseSleepMilliseconds('12px')` covered. `extractTokenUsage` with logs as array (not string)? `String(logs || '')` — old code same. Not covered but unchanged behavior... Actually wait: `extractTokenUsage` handles `logs` as array? `String([a,b])` joins with ','. Old code identical (`String(logs || '').split`). Equivalent — fine.

**o) One more check — `buildUsageAggregate` returns `atempts: tracking.samples` (same array reference as tracking). Old code did the same (`samples` local). Equivalent.

**p) `processRunLogs` tests construct `options` without `verbose`** — `state.verbose: false` set in state. OK.

**q) Check the characterization suite naming and file placement** — follows existing conventions in the same test file. Good.

**r) AGENTS.md rules**: `var` declarations, no arrow functions, no template literals, no Node APIs — the new code uses `var`, plain functions. Tests use `assert.deepEqual`, `Object.assign` — fine. Tests run in node harness AND dmtools GralJS — uses `Date.now` — fine. `loadReporterWithJava` injects Java as a var — the preamble trick — fine.

Wait — one potential GralJS concern in the TESTS: under dmtools-java harness, `loadReporter()` (no Java mock) → real `Java` global → `sleepViaJavaThread` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real thread sleep in GralJS — allowed? In smAgent's sleepMilliseconds they call Java.type the same way and tests presumably run under the same harness — smAgent.js's own tests must exercise this. It's an established pattern in this repo (smAgent comment says "same pattern as aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter"). And the PR description says dmtools-java harness ran green (4769 passed). OK.

The assertion is path-neutral (elapsed >= 2), so it passes both ways, but the busy-wait branch's true "unit" verification only happens under node. This is worth a SUGESTION? Hmm — under dmtools-java the test name is a misnomer (it actually exercises the Java path). But coverage under the node harness covers the branch. The CRAP gate runs the node harness for coverage — so branch coverage is achieved there. It's a minor observation; I'd rate it SUGESTION or skip. I'll include as a suggestion-level nit.

Under node test harness, `Java` is undefined → busy wait. Under dmtools GralJS harness, `Java` global EXISTS → `hasJavaThread()` returns true → `sleepMilliseconds(2)` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real sleep of 2ms. The test asserts `elapsed >= 2` — Thread.sleep(2) sleeps >= 2ms typically, so it passes either way. That's OK-ish but worth noting? The test name would be misleading under dmtools-java, but the assertion (elapsed >= 2) is environment-neutral. Hmm, this is a minor nit at most.

if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \

messages.preview: The `loadModule` mechanism injects mocks as `var` preamble declarations. Now let me check cross-file impact, CI workflow config, and the CRAP gate:

blocks.text:
The `loadModule` injects mocks as `var Java = _testMocks_["Java"]` — so `var Java = {}` shadows the global inside the module wrapper. In the module, `typeof Java !== 'undefined'` — since `var Java` is declared in the function scope, `typeof Java` is defined (var hoisting), even when the mock is `{}`. Wait — important subtlety: when `loadReporter()` is called WITHOUT a Java override, there's no `var Java` preamble declaration, so inside the module `typeof Java` falls back to the actual global. Under node test harness, `Java` is undefined → busy wait. Under dmtools GralJS harness, `Java` global EXISTS → `hasJavaThread()` returns true → `sleepMilliseconds(2)` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real sleep of 2ms. The test asserts `elapsed >= 2` — Thread.sleep(2) sleeps >= 2ms typically, so it passes either way. And the busy-wait test name says "busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable" — under dmtools-java, it's actually NOT busy-waiting; it sleeps via Thread.sleep. The assertion still holds (elapsed >= 2). It's a characterization test that passes in both environments, though semantically it exercises different paths depending on harness. That's OK-ish but worth noting? The test name would be misleading under dmtools-java, but the assertion (elapsed >= 2) is environment-neutral. Hmm, this is a minor nit at most.

But WAIT — there's a real concern for the `hasJavaThread is true only when the Java interop exposes type` test under the dmtools-java harness: `loadReporterWithJava({})` injects `var Java = {}` — shadowing the real global. `hasJavaThread()` → `!!(typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type)` → `typeof Java` — Java is a declared var → 'object'; `Java.type` → undefined → false. Good. And `loadReporterWithJava({ type: function() {...} })` → true. Works in both harnesses.

And `sleepMilliseconds routes positive durations to Thread.sleep under the Java interop` — injects Java mock with `type` function → `sleepViaJavaThread` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(7)` → mock records. Works in both.

Under node harness, `loadReporter()` → no `Java` var → `typeof Java === 'undefined'` → busy wait — correct path.

Under dmtools-java harness, `loadReporter()` → real Java global → hasJavaThread true → Thread.sleep — the sleep happens via Java interop. The test `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` will silently exercise the Java path instead of the busy-wait path in the canonical harness. The busy-wait branch IS covered in the node harness run. Since CI presumably runs both harnesses (ticket: "node and dmtools-java harness green"), coverage-wise the busy-wait branch gets covered by node run. This is a nuance worth a SUGESTION at most.

Actually wait, there's something more important to check — the coverage/crap gate. The crap gate runs via nyc instrument + node harness presumably (per quality.yml). Let me check the quality.yml workflow to see how the crap gate runs, to verify the busy-wait branch is covered there (node harness → Java undefined → busy wait covered). Let me check.

Also check the `while (Date.now() < end) {}` empty loop body — is an empty block statement fine for the code style? Pre-existing.

if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

messages.preview: The `loadModule` mechanism injects mocks as `var` preamble declarations. Now let me check cross-file impact, CI workflow config, and the CRAP gate:

blocks.text:
The `loadModule` injects mocks as `var Java = _testMocks_["Java"]` — so `var Java = {}` shadows the global inside the module wrapper. In the module, `typeof Java !== 'undefined'` — since `var Java` is declared in the function scope, `typeof Java` is defined (var hoisting), even when the mock is `{}`. Wait — important subtlety: when `loadReporter()` is called WITHOUT a Java override, there's no `var Java` preamble declaration, so inside the module `typeof Java` falls back to the actual global. Under node test harness, `Java` is undefined → busy wait. Under dmtools GralJS harness, `Java` global EXISTS → `hasJavaThread()` returns true → `sleepMilliseconds(2)` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real sleep of 2ms. The test asserts `elapsed >= 2` — Thread.sleep(2) sleeps >= 2ms typically, so it passes either way. And the busy-wait test name says "busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable" — under dmtools-java, it's actually NOT busy-waiting; it sleeps via Thread.sleep. The assertion still holds (elapsed >= 2). It's a characterization test that passes in both environments, though semantically it exercises different paths depending on harness. That's OK-ish but worth noting? The test name would be misleading under dmtools-java, but the assertion (elapsed >= 2) is environment-neutral. Hmm, this is a minor nit at most.

But WAIT — there's a real concern for the `hasJavaThread is true only when the Java interop exposes type` test under the dmtools-java harness: `loadReporterWithJava({})` injects `var Java = {}` — shadowing the real global. `hasJavaThread()` → `!!(typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type)` → `typeof Java` — Java is a declared var → 'object'; `Java.type` → undefined → false. Good. And `loadReporterWithJava({ type: function() {...} })` → true. Works in both harnesses.

And `sleepMilliseconds routes positive durations to Thread.sleep under the Java interop` — injects Java mock with `type` function → `sleepViaJavaThread` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(7)` → mock records. Works in both.

Under node harness, `loadReporter()` → no `Java` var → `typeof Java === 'undefined'` → busy wait — correct path.

Under dmtools-java harness, `loadReporter()` → real Java global → hasJavaThread true → Thread.sleep — the sleep happens via Java interop. The test `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` will silently exercise the Java path instead of the busy-wait path in the canonical harness. The busy-wait branch IS covered in the node harness run. Since CI presumably runs both harnesses (ticket: "node and dmtools-java harness green"), coverage-wise the busy-wait branch gets covered by node run. This is a nuance worth a SUGESTION at most.

Actually wait, there's something more important to check — the coverage/crap gate. The crap gate runs via nyc instrument + node harness presumably (per quality.yml). Let me check the quality.yml workflow to see how the crap gate runs, to verify the busy-wait branch is covered there (node harness → Java undefined → busy wait covered). Let me check.

Also check the `while (Date.now() < end) {}` empty loop body — is an empty block statement fine for the code style? Pre-existing.

if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

The doc comment says it "Returns true when the tokens sample is a replay that must be skipped" and documents the marking. It's slightly surprising but documented. Style nit — the repo convention seems tolerant. I'd call this SUGESTION.

**d) `parseCacheOptions` still parses logDownloadSleepMs inline** — duplication of sleep-parsing logic now that `parseSleepMilliseconds` exists. Two parsers for the same config value. SUGESTION: reuse. But note subtle difference: `parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0` — for '-3': -3 (truthy negative), vs parseSleepMilliseconds('-3') → 0. Gate is `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` so equivalent behavior. Reusing parseSleepMilliseconds in parseCacheOptions would be safe and would remove duplication. SUGESTION.

Hmm wait, actually let me double check: `parseSleepMilliseconds(null)` → parseInt(null) → NaN → NaN||0 → 0 → max(0,0)=0. `parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0`: null||0 → 0 → 0. Same. `undefined` same. `'500'` → 500 both. OK — equivalent for the > 0 gate. SUGESTION valid.

- `processRunLogs sleeps between downloads...` asserts `elapsed >= 5` — fine with real sleeps. 
- `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits...` asserts `elapsed >= 2` — busy wait guarantees. Under dmtools-java harness the path is Thread.sleep — still >= 2ms. OK.
- `first download must not sleep` asserts `elapsed < 100` with logDownloadSleepMs '500' — on an extremely slow CI, the non-sleep path taking >1s is nearly impossible (single function call). OK.

**f) `hasJavaThread` — `typeof Java !== 'undefined' && Java.type`** — under GralJS, `Java.type` exists. Under node with a mocked `Java = {}` (no type) → false. Matches old behavior. OK.

**g) Export surface**: `sleepViaJavaThread` / `sleepViaBusyWait` NOT exported (unlike other new helpers) — intentional? The convention per PR: "Helpers exported for direct branch coverage". These two are covered indirectly (sleepViaJavaThread via Java mock test; sleepViaBusyWait via loadReporter() under node). Consistent enough — not an issue.

**h) `newUsageTracking` — exports `applyResumeSignal`/`applyRateLimitSignal`? NOT exported** — they're covered via applyLogSignals tests. Fine.

**i) `collectFaSourceKeys(samples)` vs `usageSourceLabel(faSourceKeys)`** — could be one function, but each is trivial; CRAP-driven decomposition explains it. Not an issue.

**j) The comment on `parseResumeSignal`** says "The feedback-loop shape wins when a line matches both" — accurate.

**k) Behavior nit — `applyLogSignals` computes resume/rate-limit regexes on the raw `line` and timeout on `lower`** — matches old code exactly (old used `line.match` and `/i` regexes on line; timeout on lower). Equivalent.

**l) Any scope creep?** No — only the named functions + tests. The ticket allows refactor + tests only. Files changed: exactly 2. Baseline not committed. 

**m) `newUsageTracking()` returned object used with `deepEqual` in test — fine.

**n) Missing test?** — `sleepViaBusyWait` with ms=0? Guarded by duration<=0. `parseSleepMilliseconds('12px')` covered. `extractTokenUsage` with logs as array (not string)? `String(logs || '')` — old code same. Not covered but unchanged behavior... Actually wait: `extractTokenUsage` handles `logs` as array? `String([a,b])` joins with ','. Old code identical (`String(logs || '').split`). Equivalent — fine.

**o) One more check — `buildUsageAggregate` returns `atempts: tracking.samples` (same array reference as tracking). Old code did the same (`samples` local). Equivalent.

**p) `processRunLogs` tests construct `options` without `verbose`** — `state.verbose: false` set in state. OK.

**q) Check the characterization suite naming and file placement** — follows existing conventions in the same test file. Good.

**r) AGENTS.md rules**: `var` declarations, no arrow functions, no template literals, no Node APIs — the new code uses `var`, plain functions. Tests use `assert.deepEqual`, `Object.assign` — fine. Tests run in node harness AND dmtools GralJS — uses `Date.now` — fine. `loadReporterWithJava` injects Java as a var — the preamble trick — fine.

Wait — one potential GralJS concern in the TESTS: under dmtools-java harness, `loadReporter()` (no Java mock) → real `Java` global → `sleepViaJavaThread` calls `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)` — real thread sleep in GralJS — allowed? In smAgent's sleepMilliseconds they call Java.type the same way and tests presumably run under the same harness — smAgent.js's own tests must exercise this. It's an established pattern in this repo (smAgent comment says "same pattern as aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter"). And the PR description says dmtools-java harness ran green (4769 passed). OK.

The assertion is path-neutral (elapsed >= 2), so it passes both ways, but the busy-wait branch's true "unit" verification only happens under node. This is worth a SUGESTION? Hmm — under dmtools-java the test name is a misnomer (it actually exercises the Java path). But coverage under the node harness covers the branch. The CRAP gate runs the node harness for coverage — so branch coverage is achieved there. It's a minor observation; I'd rate it SUGESTION or skip. I'll include as a suggestion-level nit.

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

💡 **SUGGESTION: two parsers now exist for `logDownloadSleepMs` — consider reusing `parseSleepMilliseconds`**

This PR introduces `parseSleepMilliseconds` (clamp unparseable/non-positive to 0), but the pre-existing inline parse of the same config value in `parseCacheOptions` (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:912) is untouched:

```javascript
logDownloadSleepMs: parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0,
```

Behavior today is equivalent for the `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` gate in `processRunLogs` (both collapse junk/negative to a no-sleep value), so this is not a correctness issue. But two clamping idioms for one option invites drift — e.g. someone "fixing" the double-parse in one place and not the other. Folding `parseCacheOptions` onto `parseSleepMilliseconds` would leave a single parser for the value. Out of this PR's no-behavior-change scope if done carelessly (`parseCacheOptions` is exported and asserted in tests), so fine to defer — just flagging the duplication this refactor created.

💡 **SUGGESTION: busy-wait test name vs. the path it exercises under the canonical dmtools harness**

`sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` loads the reporter via `loadReporter()` — no `Java` mock. That is path-dependent per harness:

- **node harness** (also what the crap4js coverage gate runs): no global `Java` → `typeof Java === 'undefined'` → `sleepViaBusyWait` genuinely exercised.
- **canonical dmtools-java harness**: the real GralJS `Java` global exists, so `hasJavaThread()` is true and the test actually sleeps via `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)`.

The assertion (`elapsed >= 2`) is path-neutral and stays green either way, and the busy-wait branch is *deterministically* covered in both harnesses by the adjacent `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when Java.type is absent even with Java defined` test (`loadReporterWithJava({})`). So nothing is unverified — the only nit is that the test name overstates what it proves under dmtools, and the `typeof Java === 'undefined'` branch of `hasJavaThread` is only reachable under node (fine for the gate, which runs node). Either accept it as-is or rename to something path-neutral like "pauses for the requested duration without the Java interop mock".

if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

```javascript

```

Behavior today is equivalent for the `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` gate in `processRunLogs` (both collapse junk/negative to a no-sleep value), so this is not a correctness issue. Folding `parseCacheOptions` onto `parseSleepMilliseconds` would leave a single parser for the value. Out of this PR's no-behavior-change scope if done carelessly (`parseCacheOptions` is exported and asserted in tests), so fine to defer — just flagging the duplication this refactor created.

if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: two parsers now exist for `logDownloadSleepMs` — consider reusing `parseSleepMilliseconds`**

This PR introduces `parseSleepMilliseconds` (clamp unparseable/non-positive to 0), but the pre-existing inline parse of the same config value in `parseCacheOptions` (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:912) is untouched:

```javascript
logDownloadSleepMs: parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0,
```

Behavior today is equivalent for the `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` gate in `processRunLogs` (both collapse junk/negative to a no-sleep value), so this is not a correctness issue. But two clamping idioms for one option invites drift — e.g. someone "fixing" the double-parse in one place and not the other. Folding `parseCacheOptions` onto `parseSleepMilliseconds` would leave a single parser for the value. Out of this PR's no-behavior-change scope if done carelessly (`parseCacheOptions` is exported and asserted in tests), so fine to defer — just flagging the duplication this refactor created.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: busy-wait test name vs. the path it exercises under the canonical dmtools harness**

`sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` loads the reporter via `loadReporter()` — no `Java` mock. That is path-dependent per harness:

- **node harness** (also what the crap4js coverage gate runs): no global `Java` → `typeof Java === 'undefined'` → `sleepViaBusyWait` genuinely exercised.
- **canonical dmtools-java harness**: the real GralJS `Java` global exists, so `hasJavaThread()` is true and the test actually sleeps via `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)`.

The assertion (`elapsed >= 2`) is path-neutral and stays green either way, and the busy-wait branch is *deterministically* covered in both harnesses by the adjacent `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when Java.type is absent even with Java defined` test (`loadReporterWithJava({})`). So nothing is unverified — the only nit is that the test name overstates what it proves under dmtools, and the `typeof Java === 'undefined'` branch of `hasJavaThread` is only reachable under node (fine for the gate, which runs node). Either accept it as-is or rename to something path-neutral like "pauses for the requested duration without the Java interop mock".

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: two parsers now exist for `logDownloadSleepMs` — consider reusing `parseSleepMilliseconds`**

This PR introduces `parseSleepMilliseconds` (clamp unparseable/non-positive to 0), but the pre-existing inline parse of the same config value in `parseCacheOptions` (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:912) is untouched:

```javascript

```

Behavior today is equivalent for the `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` gate in `processRunLogs` (both collapse junk/negative to a no-sleep value), so this is not a correctness issue. But two clamping idioms for one option invites drift — e.g. someone "fixing" the double-parse in one place and not the other. Folding `parseCacheOptions` onto `parseSleepMilliseconds` would leave a single parser for the value. So an exception from sleep would mark the run as failed in cache and skip it. Old behavior: identical (no try/catch). So unchanged — and the ticket mandates no behavior change. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: two parsers now exist for `logDownloadSleepMs` — consider reusing `parseSleepMilliseconds`**

This PR introduces `parseSleepMilliseconds` (clamp unparseable/non-positive to 0), but the pre-existing inline parse of the same config value in `parseCacheOptions` (js/aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js:912) is untouched:

```javascript
logDownloadSleepMs: parseInt(custom.logDownloadSleepMs || 0, 10) || 0,
```

Behavior today is equivalent for the `options.logDownloadSleepMs > 0` gate in `processRunLogs` (both collapse junk/negative to a no-sleep value), so this is not a correctness issue. But two clamping idioms for one option invites drift — e.g. someone "fixing" the double-parse in one place and not the other. Folding `parseCacheOptions` onto `parseSleepMilliseconds` would leave a single parser for the value. Out of this PR's no-behavior-change scope if done carelessly (`parseCacheOptions` is exported and asserted in tests), so fine to defer — just flagging the duplication this refactor created.

`sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when the Java interop is unavailable` loads the reporter via `loadReporter()` — no `Java` mock. That is path-dependent per harness:

- **canonical dmtools-java harness**: the real GralJS `Java` global exists, so `hasJavaThread()` is true and the test actually sleeps via `Java.type('java.lang.Thread').sleep(2)`.

The assertion (`elapsed >= 2`) is path-neutral and stays green either way, and the busy-wait branch is *deterministically* covered in both harnesses by the adjacent `sleepMilliseconds busy-waits when Java.type is absent even with Java defined` test (`loadReporterWithJava({})`). So nothing is unverified — the only nit is that the test name overstates what it proves under dmtools, and the `typeof Java === 'undefined'` branch of `hasJavaThread` is only reachable under node (fine for the gate, which runs node).
